summary: Governor O'Callaghan expressed concern that local and state government needs would be ignored in implementing Executive Order 11644, noting that Nevada is 87% federally owned and its residents have historically enjoyed open public lands. He urged the Secretary of the Interior to consult local entities—specifically county commissioners and elected city officials in all 17 Nevada counties—before closing or restricting any areas to off-road vehicles. He also called for public hearings in each county seat prior to implementation, warning that failure to consider local needs could prompt Congressional intervention.

statement.text:
MIKE O'CALLAGHAN GOVERNOR
THE STATE OF NEVADA

EXECUTIVE CHAMBER

CARSON CITY, NEVADA 89701
July 3, 1972
Action Office...................................
The Honorable Rogers C. B. Morton Secretary of the Interior Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Secretary:
I have recently had the opportunity to review your letter of May 5, 1972, instructing your assistant secretaries of Public Land Management, Fish and Wild Life and Parks, and Water and Power of departmental policy on off-road vehicle use on federal lands.
I have great concern that in implementing the President's Executive Order 11644, dated February 8, 1972, that consideration of local and state government needs will be ignored by your administrators. As you well know, Nevada is 87 percent federally owned and the people of Nevada have historically enjoyed the great open spaces. I urge you to seek advice and council of local entities prior to closing or restricting any areas to offroad vehicles.
In Nevada, I believe that the County Commissioners of the 17 counties plus the elected city officials in these counties should all receive copies of the Draft Environmental Statement immediately so they may make written comments to you. Furthermore, hearings by the Department of Interior should be held in each county seat prior to the implementation of Executive Order 11644 pertaining to use of off-road vehicles on the public lands.
I feel that unless the needs and desires of the local people are given proper consideration, that eventually Congress will step in and prescribe off-road management practices for all federal land managing agencies.
I look forward to you advising your staff of this important need.
Sincerely,
12
Governor of Neva
